column5: the session and process-group semantics a late-forked child uses to leave the caller's group (scope: the syscall's own contract; the util-linux setsid(1) command's fork-versus-exec behaviour stays S328)
column6: § DESCRIPTION, man-pages 6.19 (2026-06-05) served by man7.org; fetched HTTP 200, 11555 bytes, sha256 52cbc1904742df69556104f71d3279f93581756579881c85cee8e37be37c7f30; rendered lines 80-88 (DESCRIPTION) and 111 (NOTES); the same text is present in the host's installed setsid(2) man page /usr/share/man/man2/setsid.2.gz (sha256 cf33e3d8ec282d9df4bfcc2d5a582b346e1f16501edaba46d1c51fdae23895b4)
column7: a setsid'd child is in its own new session and is the only process in it, so a group-directed signal to the caller's group or session cannot reach it; this is the semantics the r84 latefork stub relies on when it calls setsid, and the page states it without mentioning any signal-delivery policy

column5: what the /proc/<pid>/stat field list says about the ppid the descendant walk keys on and about the fields' access mode (scope: the file's own field list and its ptrace access-mode caveat; the field-6/field-22 attribution stays S075 and the kernel emission stays S332)
column6: § DESCRIPTION, man-pages 6.19 (2026-02-08) served by man7.org; fetched HTTP 200, 20647 bytes, sha256 0f04d78946538fd84db1536845abeb236da51a04844989f34ea7ee7cb0b6700f; rendered lines 77-84 (field list preamble and the ptrace access-mode caveat) and 126-128 (field 4 ppid)

column7: REJECTED: the shipped timeout(1) page mentions no process group and no session at all (zero occurrences of "group" and of "session" in the rendered page), so it cannot ground the group semantics the C2 repair rests on; S326 already carries that scope from the implementation. flip: a coreutils manual revision whose timeout(1) section states that the command is run in a new process group, which would make this page the primary source for that scope

column2: Papadakis et al., "Mutation Testing Advances: An Analysis and Survey" (Advances in Computers 112, 2019) — author preprint https://mutationtesting.uni.lu/survey.pdf
column5: the mutation-testing convention C1's clause-kill battery reuses: a mutant is killed when a test distinguishes it from the original, and the kill ratio is the reported score (scope: the method's definitions only; the lane's own five-mutant kill counts stay S335)
column6: § 2 Background, PDF pages 6 and 8 (printed pages 6 and 8 of the preprint); fetched HTTP 200, 1129278 bytes, sha256 63b7bfca877cd4661cb24e93fbfe1757a2740b39fb65ee3a79eb17e36215f023; the preprint is dated December 14, 2017; the published chapter is DOI 10.1016/bs.adcom.2018.03.015
column7: mutation testing's own terms are that a test which distinguishes a mutant's behaviour from the original kills it, and that the mutation score is the ratio of mutants so killed; the r84 battery's killed_r84=5 and killed_r83=0 are counts in exactly that convention, so a population that kills no mutant certifies no clause
